author: curriculum-architect
songSummary: Practices finding C, a short-short-long gallop rhythm, finger order, counting to four and keeping up together, with Rossini's famous galloping music.

classes.title: Saddle up on C
classes.goal: Find C by the two black keys and rest the right hand ready to ride.

mathTarget.parentLine: C always sits just left of the two black keys

classes.parentPrompt: Point to two black keys; help your child put the thumb on C, just left of them.
classes.childAction: Thumb on C, fingers curved, ready to gallop.
classes.bridge: C is the saddle, just left of the two black keys; your hand sits on it.

intro.caption: Find the saddle: C
intro.parentCue: point to the two black keys first

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: finding C and placing the hand.

classes.title: Ta-ta tah, gallop!
classes.goal: Play the gallop on G with finger 5: two quick taps, then one longer tap.

mathTarget.parentLine: Two quick taps fit in the time of one long tap

classes.parentPrompt: Say 'gal-lop, horse' with the rhythm while your child taps G with finger 5.
classes.childAction: Finger 5 on G: quick, quick, long. Gal-lop, horse!
classes.bridge: Two quick taps are hooves landing fast; the long tap is the horse leaping.

intro.caption: Gal-lop, horse! Gal-lop, horse!
intro.parentCue: say it, then pat it on your knees

games.caption: Gal-lop, horse, gal-lop, horse
games.parentCue: Say the words with each lit key

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: two quick taps and one long tap.

classes.title: 1-2-3 or 3-1-2?
classes.goal: Hear that Part 1 ends with fingers 1-2-3 and Part 2 mixes them: 3-1-2.

mathTarget.parentLine: Same three fingers, in a different order

classes.parentPrompt: Touch your child's fingers 1, 2, 3 in order, then 3, 1, 2, saying the numbers.
classes.childAction: Play C-D-E with 1-2-3, then E-C-D with 3-1-2.
classes.bridge: Fingers 1, 2, 3 are three horses; first they trot in line, then they swap.

intro.caption: Three horses in a line
intro.parentCue: touch fingers 1, 2, 3 and say the numbers

games.caption: In a line: 1, 2, 3
games.parentCue: Say the finger numbers out loud

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: finger order, 1-2-3 and 3-1-2.

classes.title: The start never changes
classes.goal: Play the whole gallop slowly and notice that each part starts the same way.

mathTarget.parentLine: Every part starts with the gallop; only the last three notes change

classes.parentPrompt: Clap the gallop with your child at each start; whisper 'what comes now?' before the ending.
classes.childAction: Gallop on G, then listen: up the stairs, swap, or down?
classes.bridge: Every part rides out of the same gate on G, then takes a different path.

intro.caption: Same gallop, different endings
intro.parentCue: clap the gallop together before you start

games.caption: Tap the beat: the first line
games.parentCue: Play the blue keys; your child taps the beat

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: hearing what stays the same and what changes.

classes.title: Big jump: 5 to thumb
classes.goal: Practise the jump from G with finger 5 down to C with the thumb, slowly.

mathTarget.parentLine: Finger 5 to thumb is the widest move in the hand

classes.parentPrompt: Rest a hand lightly on your child's wrist so the hand stays still; only fingers move.
classes.childAction: Finger 5 on G, then thumb on C. Hand stays still.
classes.bridge: The hand is a little stable; G and C are the two ends of it.

intro.caption: Jump from G to C
intro.parentCue: go slowly; the hand stays in its place

games.caption: G, G, then C
games.parentCue: Say 'five, five, thumb' with each key

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: moving from finger 5 to the thumb.

classes.title: Count four, slow horse
classes.goal: Play the whole gallop slowly while the grown-up counts 1-2-3-4 in each bar.

mathTarget.parentLine: Beats come in groups of four: one, two, three, four

classes.parentPrompt: Count '1, 2, 3, 4' softly and evenly; tap your child's shoulder on 1.
classes.childAction: Play slowly and evenly while your grown-up counts to four.
classes.bridge: A slow horse takes four even steps, then starts again on one.

intro.caption: Slow horse: one, two, three, four
intro.parentCue: count slowly and evenly out loud

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: counting four beats in a bar.

classes.title: Same gallop, new house
classes.goal: Play the gallop from a higher C with the same fingers and hear it match.

mathTarget.parentLine: The same pattern still works when the hand moves up

classes.parentPrompt: Help your child find the next C to the right, by its two black keys.
classes.childAction: Move your hand to the high C and gallop again.
classes.bridge: High C is the same house up the street: same door, same rooms.

intro.caption: A new house up high
intro.parentCue: find the next two black keys to the right

games.caption: Hear the high gallop
games.parentCue: Ask: does it sound like a pony?

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: the same song in a higher place.

classes.title: Keep up with the horses
classes.goal: Play the gallop along with the music at full speed and keep going.

mathTarget.parentLine: Fitting your playing to a speed you did not choose

classes.parentPrompt: Pat the gallop on your knee beside your child; if they miss notes, keep riding.
classes.childAction: Gallop along with the music. Missed notes? Keep riding!
classes.bridge: This is the last, fastest part of Rossini's overture; ride with the band.

intro.caption: The band is riding fast!
intro.parentCue: pat the gallop on your knee to help

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: keeping up with fast music.

classes.title: Gallop home to C
classes.goal: Play the whole gallop for teddy and land the last notes home on C.

mathTarget.parentLine: The ending walks E, D, C and lands home

classes.parentPrompt: Sit teddy as the audience; cheer on the last C, then bow together.
classes.childAction: Gallop to the end, land on C, and take a bow.
classes.bridge: The last three notes, E, D, C, ride down the stairs and into the stable.

intro.caption: Big finish for teddy!
intro.parentCue: put teddy in front as the audience

classes.celebrate: Today you practiced: a whole song with a strong ending.
